title: Water of crystallisation
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the three bank points teaches water of crystallisation or the mass-loss ratio from heating a hydrated salt; they cover calorimetry, neutralisation and acid reactions.

draft.title: Water of crystallisation
card: Some salt crystals hold water molecules inside their structure. This is water of crystallisation, and the salt is called hydrated. It is written with a dot, such as CuSO4·5H2O.
Heating a hydrated salt drives off the water as vapour. The solid left behind is the anhydrous salt, which has no water in it.
The mass lost is the mass of water. The mass left is the mass of anhydrous salt. Heat until the mass stops changing, so you know all the water has gone.
Divide each mass by its molar mass to get moles. The ratio of moles of water to moles of salt gives x in the formula salt·xH2O. Round to a whole number.
draft.remember: Mass lost is water. Convert both masses to moles, then find the ratio.

a.q: A student heats a hydrated salt until its mass stops changing. What does the mass lost show?
opts: The mass of water that was in the crystals
The mass of anhydrous salt that remains
The mass of salt that has decomposed into gas
The mass of water added from the air
a.why: Heating drives off the water of crystallisation, so the mass lost equals the mass of water. The mass of anhydrous salt is what is left behind, not what is lost, so that option is the tempting reversal.
a.clue: What leaves the crucible as vapour?

b.q: Heating 4.99 g of hydrated copper sulfate leaves 3.19 g of anhydrous CuSO4 (M = 159.6 g/mol). Water has M = 18.0 g/mol. What is x in CuSO4·xH2O?
b.why: Water lost = 4.99 - 3.19 = 1.80 g, which is 0.100 mol. The salt is 3.19 ÷ 159.6 = 0.0200 mol. The ratio is 0.100 ÷ 0.0200 = 5. Using the masses 1.80 and 3.19 directly without converting to moles gives a wrong ratio.
b.clue: Find the water lost, then turn both masses into moles.

a.best: The mass of water that was in the crystals

check.summary: No problems found. The card correctly explains water of crystallisation. The calculation in (b) checks out: 1.80 g of water is 0.100 mol, 3.19 g of CuSO4 is 0.0200 mol, so x = 5.
